title: RO-MT083-WorkerPromptComposition

scope.summary:
GOAL: Build the Worker Prompt Composition engine: the deterministic assembler that turns (role overlay from MT-081/082) + (task payload, e.g. an MT contract) + (workspace context: worktree path, branch) into the COMPLETE worker spawn payload. Basis: Anthropic's multi-agent research system finding that every worker prompt must carry objective, output format, tool/source guidance, explicit task boundaries, and an effort budget — vague worker tasks caused duplicated effort. The composed prompt is hashed and recorded so any spawned worker's exact input is reproducible.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: New module src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/worker_prompt.rs (WorkerPromptComposer, ComposedWorkerPrompt, WorkerPromptSection enum, canonical serializer, hash recording), a composition-hash FR/ledger record, integration seam into the spawn path (consumed by MT-086), plus tests. No frontend edits, no migrations (hash rides existing event surfaces; if a dedicated column is needed it belongs to MT-086's attribution rows).

DETAILED SPEC:
- pub struct WorkerPromptComposer { store: HandshakeRoleStore, recorder: Arc<dyn FlightRecorder> }.
- pub struct WorkerPromptInputs { role_id: String, role_version: Option<u32>, task_payload: TaskPayload, workspace: WorkspaceContext }.
  * TaskPayload::MicroTaskContract { mt_json: serde_json::Value } (the common case: a hsk.microtask_contract@1 document) | TaskPayload::FreeformObjective { text: String }.
  * WorkspaceContext { worktree_path: String, branch: String, repo_root_display: String } — paths passed through verbatim, never re-rooted (portability).
- pub struct ComposedWorkerPrompt { sections: Vec<WorkerPromptSection>, canonical_text: String, sha256: String, role_ref: (String, u32, String) }.
- pub enum WorkerPromptSection — FIXED deterministic order (the Anthropic worker-prompt contract):
  1. RoleOverlay — the injected role body (or a reference marker when the transport injects the overlay separately per MT-082, to avoid double-injection).
  2. Objective — extracted from the task payload (for MT contracts: scope.summary GOAL line + acceptance criteria digest).
  3. OutputFormat — the expected result envelope, INCLUDING the hsk.mt_signal@1 expectation from MT-121 (workers must emit the typed MT-signal contract, not prose status).
  4. ToolGuidance — rendered from the role's tool_policy allow/deny + transport hints.
  5. Boundaries — explicit task boundaries rendered from the MT contract's scope.allowed_paths / forbidden_paths (workers get their write-fence in the prompt, mirroring the contract).
  6. EffortBudget — from model_profile.effort plus per-spawn override; explicit statement of expected depth/iteration budget.
  7. WorkspaceContext — worktree path, branch, and any session identifiers.
- Canonical serialization: sections joined with fixed headers in fixed order, LF-normalized, no timestamps or random ids inside canonical_text; sha256 computed over canonical bytes. Same inputs => byte-identical output (pure function; test proves determinism across 2 process runs).
- Delimiter-escape duty (CTRL from MT-082): any literal "<handshake-role" sequence inside task payload text is escaped before composition so payload text cannot masquerade as role framing.
- Recording: each composition emits a worker_prompt_composed record (FR event) with { role_id, role_version, overlay_sha256, composition_sha256, mt_id?, session_target }, giving reproducibility joins: registry row -> injection event (MT-082) -> composition hash -> spawned session (MT-086).

STEP-BY-STEP IMPLEMENTATION:
1. Read MT-121's hsk.mt_signal@1 contract to render the OutputFormat section accurately (exact schema id + required fields, quoted in the prompt).
2. Implement WorkerPromptSection + fixed-order composer with canonical LF serializer; forbid nondeterministic content in canonical_text by construction (no clock/rand imports in the module; test greps).
3. Implement MT-contract extraction: objective from scope.summary, boundaries from allowed_paths/forbidden_paths, acceptance digest; tolerate missing optional fields with explicit "NOT SPECIFIED" markers rather than omission (stable shape).
4. Implement tool-policy rendering from hsk.handshake_role@1 tool_policy.
5. Implement effort-budget rendering with per-spawn override parameter.
6. Implement delimiter escaping for payload text.
7. Hash + FR worker_prompt_composed event wiring.
8. Tests: determinism (same inputs twice => same sha256), section-order pin test, mt_signal expectation presence test, boundary-rendering test against a real MT contract fixture, escape test, missing-field stability test.
forbidden_paths: app/src/** except named IPC read surfaces
.GOV/** (role protocols are read-only source material; importer reads, never writes)
acceptance_criteria: ComposedWorkerPrompt always contains the seven sections in the fixed order: RoleOverlay(or marker), Objective, OutputFormat, ToolGuidance, Boundaries, EffortBudget, WorkspaceContext.
OutputFormat section quotes the hsk.mt_signal@1 expectation (schema id + required fields) from MT-121.
Boundaries section renders the source MT contract's allowed_paths and forbidden_paths verbatim.
Composition is deterministic: identical inputs produce byte-identical canonical_text and identical sha256 across two independent runs.
canonical_text contains no timestamps, random ids, or machine-local absolute paths other than the passed-through WorkspaceContext values.
Literal role-delimiter sequences in task payload text are escaped in the composed output.
Every composition records a worker_prompt_composed FR event with composition_sha256 joined to role id/version/overlay_sha256.
When the transport injects the overlay separately (MT-082 Claude append-file), the RoleOverlay section is a reference marker, not a duplicate of the overlay body (no double-injection).
proof_targets: grep -nE 'SystemTime|Instant::now|rand::' src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/worker_prompt.rs | wc -l  # expect 0 in canonical path
expected_tests: boundary rendering test from real MT-contract fixture
implementation_notes: Anthropic multi-agent research system (verified basis): worker prompts lacking objective/output-format/tool-guidance/boundaries/effort-budget caused duplicated effort and gap coverage failures — the section list is the productized form of that finding.
The composer is a pure function over its inputs; injection side effects (temp files, args) stay in MT-082, spawn side effects in MT-086.
MT contract fixtures for tests should be vendored minimal JSON documents, not reads of .GOV/ paths (forbidden; keeps tests hermetic and portable).
Reference-marker form for RoleOverlay: "[role {id}@v{version} sha256:{h} injected via {transport}]" — pinned in tests.
Effort budget wording should be explicit and bounded (e.g. expected tool-call scale), not vague adverbs; this is what the research flags as the duplication driver.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Pure backend composition engine; worker_prompt_composed FR events + composition hashes are the trace projection. Operator-visible role surfaces are MT-085.

user_manual_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Internal composition layer consumed by the spawn flow; documented for operators in the MT-086 spawn-surface manual entry (which names the seven-section contract).

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: internal_diagnostics/Palmistry not yet shipped in wtc-multi-model-orchestration-v1; worker_prompt_composed FR event is the Tier-1 evidence surface.

risk_if_missed: Workers get ad-hoc prompts: no objective/output-format/boundary/effort discipline, no hsk.mt_signal@1 expectation, duplicated effort across parallel workers (the exact failure Anthropic documented), and no reproducibility hash tying a session to its exact input.

risks: RISK-1: Nondeterministic composition — timestamps, map-iteration order, or machine-local paths leak into canonical_text, breaking the reproducibility hash and making audit joins meaningless.
RISK-2: Double role injection — overlay injected by transport (MT-082) AND embedded in the composed prompt, doubling role text, burning context, and creating two divergent role copies.
RISK-3: Boundary drift — the Boundaries section paraphrases instead of quoting the MT contract's allowed/forbidden paths, so the worker's in-prompt fence disagrees with the contract fence.
RISK-4: Payload spoofing — task payload text containing role-delimiter or section-header sequences forges apparent role/section authority inside the composed prompt.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): pure-function composer, LF-normalized canonical serializer, no clock/rand in module (grep proof), determinism double-run test.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): RoleOverlay section becomes a reference marker whenever the transport carries the overlay; test asserts overlay body appears at most once across injection+composition.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): Boundaries rendered verbatim from contract fields with a fixture test diffing prompt lines against contract arrays.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): delimiter/section-header escaping for payload text with an adversarial fixture test.

research_provenance.source: Anthropic multi-agent research system engineering findings (verified: worker prompts must carry objective, output format, tool/source guidance, explicit task boundaries, effort budget; vague tasks caused duplicated effort) + MT-121 hsk.mt_signal@1 contract seam + MT-082 injection strategies + inspected swarm_orchestration spawn path (coordinator.rs spawn_session, operator_chat.rs build_spawn_request).
corrections: Output format = typed hsk.mt_signal@1 expectation, not prose 'report back' language.
Boundaries come from the MT contract, giving parity between the prompt fence and the governance fence.
Composition hash + FR record makes every worker's exact input reproducible — the productized form of repo-gov's startup-capsule discipline.
